newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch corporate profits up 18 pct in 1995 - CBS.
newsitem.headline: Dutch corporate profits up 18 pct in 1995 - CBS.

text.p: Total 1995 net profits of Dutch big companies, excluding the financial sector, showed a year-on-year growth of 18 percent to 42.9 billion guilders, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.
"An important part of this rise was caused by the chemicals and minerals sectors, where total net profits grew by 3.6 billion guilders to 12.8 billion," it said in a statement.

The bureau added that the services sector was the only business segment where net profits fell. This sector had a total profit of 1.3 billion guilders, eight percent below the 1.5 billion posted in 1994.

The CBS said 258 of the 1,562 companies polled suffered a net loss in 1995 with negative results totalling 3.7 billion guilders. This excluded the 1995 loss of aircraft maker Fokker which went bankrupt earlier this year.
In 1994, 238 companies posted a total loss of 4.3 billion guilders.

The bureau said the Dutch companies' 1995 net result as a percentage of shareholders' equity rose to 15.7 from 14.6 percent in 1994. The food sector was most profitable with a percentage of 22.5 but the transport, storage and communication sectors showed a yield of only 11 percent.
